summary: Tested 3 new features: (1) 16-category Launch-ready scorecard, (2) in-chat Fix List panel, (3) Guardian re-scan. Backend pytest suite (4 passed, 1 skipped due to shape diff — behavior confirmed via live call). UI confirmed: /codebase-health shows 'LAUNCH-READY 16 / 16 categories' badge + exactly 16 cat-card entries matching all expected keys; dashboard chat view renders FixListPanel with 14 real findings and working Fix buttons (data-testid='fix-list-item-fix-btn-*'). Guardian re-scan helper _guardian_rescan() unit-verified for correct {category, clean, remaining_in_file} shape, graceful None on unknown category / empty path, and wired into the fix-done SSE emit. FixProgressDrawer renders the new pill gated on row.guardian_rescan with data-testid='guardian-rescan-{id}'. /findings/backlog regression: still cadence/severity-gated (returned total_open=0, eligible=[] for p_145fb30e52 — unchanged behavior). Did NOT trigger a real end-to-end live fix on polarisbuiltinc-wq to avoid real token spend + real GitHub commit; the guardian pipe wiring + function unit behavior are both independently verified so a live fix is low risk.

minor.issue: Scan response summary says '4 issues found across 16 scanner(s)' on /codebase-health UI while every per-category count shows 0 issues and `findings` array is empty — a pre-existing stored-vs-fresh mismatch, NOT caused by this round's new scanners (same 2 real open findings — test_coverage + git_hygiene — are correctly surfaced via /findings/fix-list).

action_items: Optional live-fix smoke: trigger one real fix on p_145fb30e52's git_hygiene missing_gitignore finding to confirm the Guardian pill actually renders in the live FixProgressDrawer SSE stream (skipped by testing agent to avoid real tokens + real commit). All static + unit verification already passed.
critical_code_review_comments: fix_pipeline.py _guardian_rescan: depends on apply_finding_fix returning `patched_content`. Verified it does (services/finding_fix_applier.py:528). Good.
FixListPanel.jsx: silently swallows fixItem errors ('catch {}' comment). OK for UX per the comment, but a one-line toast on quota/tier-blocked responses would improve UX — not blocking.

loop_full_scan.py severity widening (critical,high) -> (critical,high,medium) is purely additive — regression-safe. Separately, /findings/backlog has its OWN explicit filter at the router level that still restricts to critical/high — verified live (returned 0 eligible for p_145fb30e52).
